help.en: A part that actors play in the business, such as order clerk, independent of who fills it.
A repeatable set of activities that produces a result for a customer or for the organisation.
How many services, components and interfaces serve it.
A point where an application can be reached by people or other applications, such as a screen or an API, with the format it uses.
A band that gathers the elements of one layer: business, application or technology. Lines between layers stay visible across it.
A person, team or outside party that does something, such as a customer or a department.
What the business offers to its customers or to other parts of the organisation, such as ordering or invoicing.
Who uses it.
What is promised, such as opening hours.

constraints.message: = 'Business service "' + Name + '" is not realised: connect the process or application service that provides it with "Realises".'

help.en: A piece of software with its own owner and life cycle, such as a web shop or an order system.
What should happen to it: build it, invest in it, keep it as it is, move away from it, or switch it off.
How many elements it serves or realises.

constraints.message: = 'Application component "' + Name + '" is to be retired but still serves or realises ' + Supports + ' element' + (Supports == 1 ? '' : 's') + ': move them to another component first.'
= 'Application component "' + Name + '" runs nowhere: connect the node or system software it runs on with "Assigned to".'

help.en: A function that an application offers to the business or to other applications, such as order handling.

constraints.message: = 'Application service "' + Name + '" is not realised: connect the application component that provides it with "Realises".'

help.en: Data that applications use and keep, such as an order or a customer record.
How many processes, components and services access it.

constraints.message: = 'Data object "' + Name + '" is not used by anything.'

help.en: Something software runs on: a server, a virtual machine, a container platform, a cloud service or a device.
How many components and system software it runs.
Software that other software needs, such as an operating system, a database or middleware.
A network that connects nodes, such as a local network or the internet.
Offers its function to the element it points to: a service serves a process, a component serves another component, a node serves the software on it.
Makes the service or interface real: a process realises a business service, a component realises an application service or interface.
Who or what does the work or runs it: an actor fills a role, a role performs a process, a node runs software.
The process, component or service reads or writes the data object.
Something passes from one process or component to the next, such as an order.
What passes, such as "order".
The actor or process starts the next process.
The node is connected to the network, or the two are linked.
How many application components the model holds.
How many business processes the model holds.
The business, application and technology layers of an organisation and how they serve, realise and run each other.
